message.content:
Here’s a quick reference for the Canadian federal public holidays that created long‑weekends in 2023:

| Holiday | Date (2023) | Day of Week | Long‑Weekend? | Notes |
|---------|-------------|-------------|---------------|-------|
| New Year’s Day | Jan 1 (Sunday) | Sunday | **Yes** – Observed on Monday, Jan 2 | Federal holiday observed on next weekday |
| Family Day (Alberta, Saskatchewan, Ontario) | Feb 20 (Monday) | Monday | **Yes** – Creates a long‑weekend (Sat 18–Mon 20) | Only in those provinces |
| Good Friday | Apr 7 (Friday) | Friday | **Yes** – Creates a long‑weekend (Fri 7–Sun 9) | Observed nationwide |
| Victoria Day | May 22 (Monday) | Monday | **Yes** – Creates a long‑weekend (Sat 20–Mon 22) | Nationwide |
| Canada Day | Jul 1 (Saturday) | Saturday | **No** – Observed on Monday, Jul 3 | Observed on next weekday |
| Labour Day | Sep 4 (Monday) | Monday | **Yes** – Creates a long‑weekend (Sat 2–Mon 4) | Nationwide |
| Thanksgiving | Oct 10 (Monday) | Monday | **Yes** – Creates a long‑weekend (Sat 8–Mon 10) | Nationwide |
| Remembrance Day | Nov 11 (Thursday) | Thursday | **No** – Not a statutory holiday for most workers | Some employers observe |
| Christmas Day | Dec 25 (Monday) | Monday | **Yes** – Creates a long‑weekend (Sat 23–Mon 25) | Nationwide |
| Boxing Day | Dec 26 (Tuesday) | Tuesday | **No** – Creates a short weekend (Tue 26–Thu 28) | Nationwide |

### How to programmatically retrieve this info

If you’re building an app, you can use the `holidays` Python package (or similar libraries in other languages) to generate holiday calendars for Canada:

```python
import holidays

canada_holidays = holidays.Canada(years=2023)
for date, name in sorted(canada_holidays.items()):
    print(date, name)
```

This will give you all federal holidays for 2023. If you need provincial holidays (e.g., British Columbia’s “Natal Day” or Quebec’s “Saint‑Jean‑Baptiste Day”), you’ll need to add the appropriate province flag (`Canada(provinces='BC')`, etc.).
